AN ILLUSTRATED ISSUE MAP

One library, six neighbourhoods

Thirty workplaces across six neighbourhoods connect lending, learning, stock and delivery. Five shared applications support them, with a common runtime, database and gateway.

How do local branches and shared technology deliver one regional library service?

THE ISSUE, IN WORDS

How do local branches and shared technology deliver one regional library service?

Thirty workplaces across six neighbourhoods connect lending, learning, stock and delivery. Five shared applications support them, with a common runtime, database and gateway.

SCENARIO 01

A reader crosses neighbourhoods

Starting condition. Northbank has the chosen book; the Riverside reading group is open.

  1. Find the collection

    The welcome team directs the reader to the Northbank collection.

  2. Join another neighbourhood

    The reader takes the connecting streets to the Riverside learning centre and joins the group.

Outcome. The reader reaches the Riverside learning team with a book from Northbank.

SCENARIO 02

A book from another branch

Starting condition. The local branch lacks the requested copy; Harbour has one available.

  1. Register the request

    Northbank staff check membership and record the reader’s reservation.

  2. Find a regional copy

    Reservations checks the shared catalogue and identifies the Harbour copy.

  3. Prepare and deliver

    Harbour prepares the copy, schedules it and delivers it to Northbank.

  4. Confirm and notify

    Northbank confirms receipt. The notices service sends the pickup message through the gateway.

Outcome. The receiving branch confirms arrival before the reader is notified.

SCENARIO 03

The shared foundation

Starting condition. All six branches use the shared applications.

  1. Shared discovery

    Each collection team searches the same regional catalogue.

  2. Common runtime and records

    The applications share runtime and storage. An interruption here affects several branch activities.

Outcome. The operating team can trace branch dependencies through services to runtime and records.

All places, services and relationships

01 · Northbank Welcome

Front-desk team. Welcomes readers, checks requests and connects them to branch services.

Staff check the collection before promising a pickup.

02 · Northbank Collection

Collection team. Maintains the lending collection and prepares reserved books.

A reservation is ready only after the book is located.

03 · Northbank Learning

Learning team. Runs reading groups and digital learning sessions.

Session places and facilitator availability determine the programme.

04 · Northbank Book store

Stock team. Receives, sorts and stores books moving through the regional collection.

Each transfer needs an identified destination branch.

05 · Northbank Delivery

Delivery team. Plans inter-branch deliveries and records arrival.

Branch staff confirm receipt before a book becomes ready for pickup.

S1 · Shared catalogue

Collection discovery. Lists titles and the branch holding each copy.

Branches update holdings after each transfer.

S2 · Reservations

Reservation coordination. Tracks a reader’s request from ordering to pickup.

A request remains pending until a copy is assigned.

S3 · Membership

Reader records. Maintains membership records used by the front desks.

Staff resolve unmatched reader records before lending.

S4 · Delivery planning

Transfer planning. Groups prepared transfers into delivery runs.

Planning uses the branch destination and ready status.

S5 · Reader notices

Pickup notifications. Sends a pickup notice after the receiving branch confirms the book.

A pending transfer must not trigger a ready notice.

T6 · Shared runtime

Application operations. Runs the shared library services.

Service availability depends on this runtime.

T7 · Library records

Data operations. Stores catalogue, membership and reservation records.

Services need consistent updates when books move.

T8 · Message gateway

External messaging. Connects notices and delivery updates to external endpoints.

Delivery acknowledgements return through the gateway.
